It is recorded as an email method with an explicit limitation that it establishes a working mailbox and NOT the business — the same treatment given to the PagineGialle VAT field, where a required form value was not allowed to become a verification claim.  NOT ASSERTED: owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic, and the operator’s ranking and lead-generation claims.

name: Approved Business
description: A UK business-to-business directory operated by Approved Business Ltd. Listing is organised as packages rather than a single free entry: a free package exists, but the operator attaches a twelve-month contract to it and places free listings below paid ones.
bestFor: UK business-to-business suppliers wanting a categorised trade listing with an enquiry form.
Businesses comparing what a free directory package actually withholds, since the operator sets the tiers out feature by feature.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses unwilling to accept a twelve-month term on a free listing.
Anyone expecting a free listing to carry a link to their website. The operator lists that as a paid-tier feature.
reviewProcess: The operator states that publication of submitted material is at its sole discretion and that it may make additions or deletions before publication.
pros: The operator is named consistently throughout its own terms as Approved Business Ltd, which sets out publication and licensing terms in its own name.
Every package, free included, is documented as carrying company name, address, phone number, quote form, review system and an admin console.
The tier structure is set out feature by feature, so what a free package withholds is visible before signing up rather than after.
The operator reserves an explicit editorial role over submitted material, which is a real moderation position rather than automatic publication.
cons: The free package carries a “12 month contract”. A free listing here is a term commitment, not a casual entry, and that is unusual enough to check before submitting.
A free listing is positioned last: the operator states it “Displays at the bottom of product and service pages”, with paid listings above it.
A website link is a paid feature. “Website backlink” appears in the Featured tier’s feature list and not in the free package, so no link benefit is documented for a free listing and none is asserted.
The operator also sells SEO, website design, email marketing, video production and social media services, so the directory sits inside a marketing-services business rather than standing alone.

Publication is discretionary and editable by the operator: it “may publish and make available to the public by any means any material that you submit … at their sole discretion and they shall be entitled to make additions or deletions to any such material prior to publication.”
Submitted material is licensed broadly: the terms take “a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual and worldwide licence to republish any material you submit”.
Creating a listing is confirmed; claiming an existing third-party listing is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.
A review system is documented in every package, but whether a business can respond to reviews is not, and is not asserted.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own package page and terms and conditions, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “Approved Business Ltd”, “12 month contract”, “Displays at the bottom of product and service pages” and “Website backlink” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: Approved Business Ltd, named throughout its own terms and conditions as the publishing party. LISTING CONTROL: The business selects a package and supplies material; the operator decides whether and in what form it is published. MODERATION AUTHORITY: The operator, by stated sole discretion, including additions and deletions before publication. PUBLIC INTERFACE: approvedbusiness.co.uk, with the package and registration route at /list-your-company. COST DECISION: freemium. A free package is documented and so are Featured, Premium and Premium+ tiers. The twelve-month contract attached to the free package is recorded as a limitation, not as a reason to call the tier paid — no money is documented as changing hands.  NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic. The Featured tier’s “Website backlink” wording is reported as the operator’s own product description and is NOT adopted as a link-attribute claim by this record.

name: Bizify
description: A UK business directory operated by Outrank Limited, a Middlesbrough search-marketing company. It functions as a directory with listings and reviews, but is built and marketed as a ranking instrument — and the operator’s own terms disclaim the search outcomes its marketing pages promise.
bestFor: UK-registered businesses wanting an additional free directory listing with a named, companies-house-identified operator.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses choosing a directory for search-ranking reasons. The operator’s own terms disclaim exactly that outcome.
Businesses outside the UK. The operator restricts free listings to UK-based registered businesses.
pros: The operator is fully identified in its own terms: “Bizify.co.uk is a site operated by Outrank Limited trading as “bizify” … registered in England and Wales under company number 11723162”.
The free tier is stated without qualification: “Any registered business, based in the UK, can sign up for a free business listing on bizify.”
The creation route is documented rather than implied — “All you need to do is sign in and follow the on screen instructions to create your listing.”

Consumer reviews are part of the documented product: the operator describes users “who have used a business that is listed with bizify, and would like to leave a review of the product or service they received”.
cons: The operator contradicts its own marketing. The site promises that listings “rank” and are “built to rank too”, while the terms state: “We do not provide any warranties or guarantees as to the outcome of any of the Advertising Services, including but not limited to traffic driven to your website, orders for your goods or services, and placement of your website on any search engines.” The disclaimer is the binding text.

This is a directory operated by a search-marketing company — “Part of the Outrank Ecosystem”, with a “Free SEO report” among its own links. That context matters when judging what a listing here is for.
An account is required before a listing can be created: the submission route redirects to a login page, so this is not an anonymous submission.
The FAQ refers in passing to having “claimed your listing”, but no claim workflow is documented anywhere, so claiming is NOT asserted and the listing action is recorded as create only.
The operator gives two different registered addresses for itself on the same site — one in its terms and another in its FAQ — which is a small but real inconsistency in its own disclosures.
The audience and customer figures on the site are the operator’s own claims and have not been independently checked.
Whether verification is required, and by what method, is not documented, so nothing about verification is asserted.
Reviews exist, but whether a business can respond to them is not documented and is not asserted.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own terms and conditions, about page and FAQ, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “operated by Outrank Limited”, “company number 11723162”, “can sign up for a free business listing on bizify” and “We do not provide any warranties or guarantees as to the outcome” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: Outrank Limited, trading as bizify, named with its company number in the platform’s own terms and separately in its FAQ. LISTING CONTROL: The business signs in and creates and manages its own listing. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented. PUBLIC INTERFACE: bizify.co.uk, with the creation route at /add-new-company, which redirects to a login. ACCEPTANCE DECISION: published, unlike Brownbook. Brownbook was rejected because its own self-description makes search-engine marketing the PRODUCT. Bizify’s documented product is a directory listing with reviews and a free tier, operated by a search-marketing company that markets ranking benefits alongside it. The distinction is between a platform whose function is selling search outcomes and a platform that is a directory sold on search-outcome language. The remedy chosen here is publication with the contradiction quoted, because the operator’s own disclaimer is more useful to a reader than silence.  MARKETING CLAIM NOT ADOPTED: the ranking and SERP-performance claims on the about page are recorded as claims and refuted from the operator’s own terms.  NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic.
